usage: This phrase is used to imply that only those who have prior knowledge or experience will understand a particular situation or reference.
It often carries a tone of exclusivity or inside knowledge, suggesting an unspoken bond among those 'in the know.'
The phrase can be used to respond subtly when a topic is sensitive or not appropriate for everyone to fully grasp.
It is commonly used in casual conversations, especially among friends or communities sharing common experiences or jokes.
This expression usually appears at the end of a sentence or comment to emphasize the implied understanding.
